Adulate

AJ-oo-layt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To adulate to praise someone excessively and fawningly.

The courtiers would adulate the young prince's every decision, however small.

Worked Example

Employees who wanted to get ahead learned to adulate their notoriously vain manager at every meeting.

Adulate describes fawning, often insincere praise heaped on someone who holds power over the person doing the praising.

How Strong Is It? — compliment → adulate → grovel

compliment vs. adulate

compliment vs. adulate: Complimenting someone is a normal, healthy form of praise; adulating them crosses into fawning excess.

grovel vs. adulate

grovel vs. adulate: To grovel is to abase yourself completely before someone, a step beyond simply adulating them.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — adul

root — adul: to fawn on (Latin (adulari))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make, to cause to become (Latin (-are))

Put it together

Put it together: adul ("to fawn on") + -ate ("to make") = to fawn on with excessive praise.

Use the root in a new word: adulation

Use the root in a new word: adulation: The same root gives us "adulation," the noun for excessive, fawning praise.
